newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece says Albanian rebels should attend talks.
newsitem.headline: Greece says Albanian rebels should attend talks.

text.p: Greece said on Wednesday southern Albanian rebels should be included in all-party talks in Tirana aimed at ending a violent uprising in the impoverished Balkan country.

Asked if Greece believed the insurgents controlling the south should participate in negotiations between embattled President Sali Berisha and opposition parties, government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters: "Of course. The insurgents cannot be ignored."
The rebels have united under an umbrella group called the National Committee for People's Salvation, which called for Berisha's resignation and a separate seat at the negotiating table.
Greece, which has watched with concern as the Albanian crisis unfoldis at its northern border, said it was speaking to all sides in the dispute in an effort to avert further violence.
Reppas said only a government of the widest possible acceptance would be able to lead Albania out of the crisis.
An armed uprising has swept southern Albania over the past two weeks, with dozens of towns and villages being taken over by rebels opposing Berisha.
The crisis was triggered when popular investment schemes collapsed in January, wiping out the savings of thousands of Albanians.
Weapons have been looted from army arsenals over the past week and rebels in the southwest corner of Albania are now heavily armed, including artillery and tanks.
Gangs of armed men also roam the countryside uncontrolled and residents of all ages have joined in looting state property.
